container: The gig economy refers to a labor market characterized by short-term, flexible jobs often facilitated by digital platforms. Workers in this economy, known as gig workers, typically take on freelance or contract work rather than traditional full-time employment. Popular examples include ride-sharing drivers, delivery personnel, and freelance writers. These platforms connect workers directly with customers, allowing for on-demand services. While the gig economy offers flexibility and autonomy, it also raises concerns about job security, benefits, and fair pay. Many gig workers lack access to health insurance, retirement plans, and unemployment protections. The rise of automation and artificial intelligence may further impact job stability in this sector. Policymakers are exploring regulations to better protect gig workers while preserving the flexibility that makes this model appealing. Understanding the gig economy is crucial as it reshapes how people work and earn income in the modern digital age.
